key_insight: ProxyPose reframes 6-DoF pose tracking as a video-to-video translation problem, letting the model infer pose directly from monocular video without needing extra inputs like depth, masks, or 3D models. This makes pose tracking more practical for challenging real-world surfaces such as transparent, reflective, textureless, or deformable objects.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of tracking the full 6-DoF pose of objects and surfaces from a single video stream, especially when traditional methods fail without auxiliary 3D information or hand-crafted priors.
method: Transforms the pose-tracking task into video-to-video translation rather than explicit geometry estimation.
Uses only monocular video as input, avoiding reliance on depth maps, object masks, or 3D models.
Learns to map video observations to pose-relevant outputs in a way that is robust to visually difficult surface types.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ProxyPose suggests a simpler and more flexible path to pose tracking in settings where collecting 3D annotations or sensor data is expensive. It could improve deployment in robotics, AR/VR, and vision systems operating on hard-to-model objects.

paper_title: ProxyPose: 6-DoF Pose Tracking via Video-to-Video Translation
paper_authors: Ruihang Zhang, Felix Taubner, Pooja Ravi, Kiriakos N. Kutulakos, David B. Lindell
